name: Find unused Microsoft 365 licenses with Microsoft Graph and email a weekly report

## Find unused Microsoft 365 licenses with Microsoft Graph and email a weekly report

### How it works

This workflow runs every Monday at 8:00 to audit Microsoft 365 license usage. It calls Microsoft Graph to retrieve subscribed SKUs and users with their assigned licenses, then analyzes the data to identify unused licenses. Finally, it emails a weekly report with the license findings.

### Setup steps

- Configure Microsoft Graph authentication for the HTTP Request nodes, typically with an Azure app registration that has permission to read subscribed SKUs and users/license details.
- Verify the Microsoft Graph endpoints and pagination handling in the subscribed SKUs and users request nodes for the size of your tenant.
- Edit the configuration section in the Analyze Licenses code node, including any SKU mappings, thresholds, or report formatting settings.
- Connect the Gmail node to the sending account and set the report recipients, subject, and email body fields.

### Customization

Adjust the schedule, license SKU mapping, unused-license criteria, and email recipients to match your organization’s reporting needs.

## Schedule and collect data

Starts the workflow every Monday morning and retrieves Microsoft 365 subscribed SKU/license inventory plus user license assignments from Microsoft Graph.

## Analyze and email report

Calculates unused or underused Microsoft 365 licenses from the Graph data, formats the findings, and sends the weekly report by email.

### 🚀 Running an MSP with many client tenants?

This template covers **one tenant**. I build multi-tenant versions that loop over all your customers, reconcile against **Pax8 / distributor billing exports and your PSA**, flag count mismatches in both directions, and post a per-client summary to email/Slack/Teams — the monthly billing-reconciliation grind, automated.

Async delivery, no calls — contact links in my creator profile.
